messages:
Alex: heads up — noticed steady RSS growth on longcontext runs (12k tokens) after ~20m. not a leak per se, looks like kv cache hole accumulation / small-chunk churn.
Marta: can you paste the numbers? rough delta and where it shows up (heap vs rss)?
Alex: yeah, quick capture from canary yesterday: 
```
time  start_rss_mb  end_rss_mb  kv_entries  hole_count  avg_block_bytes
0m    6200         6200        0           0           -
20m   6200         6420        21k         8.9k        256
40m   6200         6605        23.8k       10.7k       240
60m   6200         6752        25.1k       12.0k       232
```
Alex: hole_count = free fragments that are too small to satisfy incoming allocations often; avg_block_bytes trending down.
Ryan: ok so micro-fragmentation. do we have allocator histo? distribution of free chunk sizes?
Alex: attached simplified histogram (percent of free space by size bin):
```
>64b: 42%
64-256b: 38%
256-1k: 12%
>1k: 8%
```
Marta: that 42% under 64b is alarming. matches long-context KV usage where many tiny kv entries are left behind from short-lived contexts (~a few tokens).
Ben: could be exacerbated by our current block-size config (base=256, grow=1.25). small blocks get carved up and never coalesce because buddy-linking isn't exact.
Marta: what are the options? bigger base block will reduce meta overhead but increase waste, smaller won't help here. Thinking: lightweight compaction pass that only merges adjacent holes and prioritizes spans that yield >X bytes reclaimed. call it "slimline compactor"?
Ryan: I like a targeted compactor rather than full GC. proposal: run a sampling compaction on slices with hole_density > 0.35 and age > 5m. merge contiguous free runs up to some budget (e.g., 128KB per cycle) to avoid latency spikes.
Ben: also consider an on-alloc heuristic: if request size > remaining_in_chunk and chunk_remain < threshold, try to pull next contiguous free and coalesce opportunistically before fallback allocation. cheap fast path.
Alex: performance tradeoffs? microbench showed compaction cycle of 128KB budget adds ~0.7% p99 latency when run inline; when backgrounded with low priority thread it's ~0.1% p99 but reclaims slower.
Marta: +1 on background thread. prefer background greedy for long-running instances and inline opportunistic coalesce for tight latency cases. we can gate by SLO tag per model.
Ryan: need a metric and rollout plan: add `kv.hole_density`, `kv.compact_cycles`, `kv.bytes_reclaimed` to telemetry. dogfood on a subset of dedicated nodes, compare token cost and p99.
Alex: experiment plan draft:
- Canary A: baseline (no compactor) 24h on 10 nodes
- Canary B: slimline compactor bg thread (budget 128KB/cycle, wake every 1s) 24h on 10 nodes
- Canary C: bg + opportunistic inline coalesce (alloc fast-path) 24h on 10 nodes
Collect: RSS delta, kv_entries, hole_count, p50/p95/p99 latency, reclaim bytes/sec.
Ben: also run synthetics with longcontext chat replay to stress steady-state accumulation, and a shorter chat workload to validate no perf regress.
Marta: code sketch for compactor loop we can iterate on:
```cpp
while (!stop) {
  sleep(1s);
  for (auto& slab : slab_list) {
    if (slab.hole_density() < 0.35 || slab.age() < 300s) continue;
    size_t budget = 128*1024;
    for (auto r = slab.find_high_priority_hole_runs(); r && budget > 0; r = next) {
      size_t reclaimed = slab.merge_runs(r);
      budget -= reclaimed;
      record_metric("kv.bytes_reclaimed", reclaimed);
    }
  }
}
```
Alex: must be careful with concurrent access — use try-lock and yield quickly to avoid stalling alloc path. also prefer to compact cold slabs first.
Ryan: sounds good. last question: block-size tuning PD? maybe change base to 128 for models with many tiny kvs? would help if small entries are common. but any change needs conversion cost for existing slabs.
Ben: we can run a per-model profiling pass: run short inference trace to compute kv_size_percentiles and suggest base block. surface recommendation in console (Redwood Optimize).
Marta: I'll open an RFC with the slimline compactor algorithm + telemetry + experiment plan. Alex / Ryan / Ben can you paste any additional numbers or microbench code there?
Alex: will add allocator histo dump and the microbench.
Ryan: I'll wire up telemetry keys and dashboards.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary group created: "kv-slimline-canary" (20 nodes). scheduled at 03:00 UTC. react with :thumbsup: to acknowledge.
Ben: :thumbsup:
Marta: :thumbsup: thanks team — aim to have RFC by EOD tomorrow so eng-sre can schedule the canary.
Alex: extra note: if compaction reduces free slot count too aggressively we might increase fragmentation for other sizes — need to tune merge granularity. include a sim in RFC.
Ryan: copy. I'll add a sim harness that runs random long-context traces and reports hole evolution.
Marta: perfect. closing notes: short-lived plan + metrics + canary. will follow up in RFC thread.
